newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Taiwan buys September fuel oil at $120/T, $129/T.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan buys September fuel oil at $120/T, $129/T.

text.p: Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) has bought two 0.5-percent sulphur fuel oil cargoes for September delivery at $120 and $129 per tonne, a company source said on Wednesday.

The first 38,000-tonne low-pour cargo, bought at around $129 per tonne, will be for September 1-10 delivery and the second high-pour cargo, bought at $120 per tonne, will be for September 21-30, the source said.

"We didn't buy enough for September this time because we are not happy with the prices," said the source, adding that CPC would issue another fuel oil tender in the next few weeks for September cargoes.
In its last purchase tender, Taiwan bought two 38,000-tonne fuel oil cargoes at $132 and $123 per tonne for August delivery.

The first 0.5-percent cargo was bought at around $132 per tonne and the second 1.0-percent cargo, with an American Petroleum Institute (API) gravity of 15 degrees and a viscosity of 140-centistoke, was at about $123 per tonne.
